subject: Problem for specifying a model with spatial variable effects

messages.author: f97b0bfe799a761a
messages.subject: Problem for specifying a model with spatial variable effects
parts:
Dear INLA forum, 


We would like to implement a model where the dependent variable, which follows a Poisson distribution, depends on the following random effects and some other covariates:


y(i, j,t) = f{y(i,j,t-1),y(-i,j,t),y(-i,-j,t)} + other covariates


where i represents the space, j the sector of an economic activity and t the time. The idea is to analyse the variation of our dependent variable considering the temporal effect, the spatial effect, and the effect of an exogenous variable which depends both on the rest of the regions except i and on all the economic activities but j.

We have written the following code but we don't know how to express the effect represented by y(-i,-j,t). How can we fix it?


y_ex<-y2+y3+y4+y5

mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(coord, max.edge=c(0.08, 0.5), cutoff=0.01)

spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh, alpha=2)

data1=list(field=mesh$idx$loc,year=period,Y=y1,y=y_ex)

formula = Y ~ f(field, model=spde,diagonal=diag.eps)+f(y, ???????)+f(year,model="rw1", diagonal=diag.eps)

resultat=inla(formula,data=data1,family="poisson",control.compute=list(dic=T,cpo=TRUE),control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE,cdf=c(log(1))),control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 0.01))


Thank you very much,
